resources.string: control Pangolin tunnels, enabling and disabling tunnels at will.
Disable Always-On VPN in Android settings before disconnecting.
Keep a status notification while connected. A temporary notification may still appear when connecting or recovering. Android’s own VPN indicators are unaffected.
Allow notifications for Pangolin in Android settings to show VPN status.
All apps use the VPN. Choose apps to exclude, or pick only the apps that should use it. Takes effect on the next connect.
Every app uses the VPN except the ticked ones, which use your network directly.
Only the ticked apps (and Pangolin) use the VPN. Every other app uses your network directly, so push notifications, calls and Android Auto are not affected.
Tick the apps that should use the VPN. Until you tick at least one, every app uses it.

If Android or the battery manager closes Pangolin, bring the VPN back up: on restart, after boot and with a check every 15 minutes. Disconnecting by hand turns it off until you connect again.
Pangolin is not optimized: Android lets it run in the background.
Pangolin is optimized: Android may stop the VPN. Tap to allow background use.
Turn on Autostart for Pangolin, so MIUI lets it restart after it closes it.
Choose “No restrictions” for Pangolin. This is MIUI’s own setting, separate from Android’s battery optimization.
In the recent apps screen, long-press Pangolin and tap the lock, so “Clear all” does not close it.
Open Android’s VPN settings, tap the gear next to Pangolin and turn on Always-on VPN: Android then restarts it too. Leave “Block connections without VPN” off.
